provenance.note: Re-validation of pystatistics.multivariate (PCA + ML factor analysis) against a PyPI-installed pystatistics==5.0.0. 5.0.0 is a RENAME-ONLY release over the blessed 4.4.1 line — no statistical change to the multivariate module (pca/factor_analysis and their selectors backend=/solver=/n_components=/n_factors=/rotation= are all unchanged; the private *Params dataclasses were dropped from the package __all__ but stay importable from pystatistics.multivariate._common, and the drivers never import them). No driver edits were needed. Every CPU-side agreement number reproduces 4.4.1 BYTE-FOR-BYTE: PCA correctness vs prcomp (sdev/rotation/scores/evr identical to the last digit), the R10 hard cases (near-collinear cond~1e8, rank-deficient, wide p>>n, constant-column matched refusal — identical), and factor analysis vs factanal on 1/2/3 factors (uniquenesses/loadings/objective/chi-squared identical). The MPS randomized PCA leg was re-measured live on Apple Silicon: within the GPU_FP32 statistical-equivalence tier (top-k subspace <=0.030 deg, sdev 3e-7..1.9e-4), with the fail-loud guards (explicit solver='svd'/'gram' raise) and the no-silent-wrong condition gate (accept well-conditioned top-k, refuse ill-conditioned, force=True override) all reproduced; per-point numbers differ only at the documented fp32 GPU-reduction-nondeterminism level (same-seed not bit-identical), same per-point tier classification as 4.4.1. The CUDA (forge) studies — CF-1 gate boundary (silent_wrong_count=0), R11 precision-vs-hardware isolation, and CUDA randomized value/correctness — are CARRIED FORWARD from v4.4.1 unchanged (Forge/RTX 5070 Ti not attached to this host; 5.0.0 is rename-only so the CUDA numerics cannot have moved). Host: powerhouse (Apple Silicon M2 Max, CPU fp64 + Metal/MPS fp32, R 4.5.2, numpy+R both on Apple Accelerate BLAS). CARRY-FORWARD CF-1 remains CLEARED. F1/F2 remain CLEARED, F3 remains a documented R2 cost. BLESS-CLEAN: rename-only, no material delta, no open finding. See runs/ and findings_ledger.md.
provenance.baseline: Supersedes reports/multivariate-v4.4.1.md (the blessed FA-validated line). 4.4.1 -> 5.0.0 is a library-wide RENAME-ONLY release; the multivariate public API and numerics are unchanged, and the frozen evidence reproduces 4.4.1 (CPU byte-identical; MPS within fp32 tier; CUDA carried forward).

reference.name: R stats::prcomp / stats::factanal
reference.what: R's prcomp() (PCA via SVD of the centred/scaled data matrix) and factanal() (maximum-likelihood factor analysis). Loadings/scores are sign-aligned per component before comparison; near-degenerate/null-space directions are compared by the rotation-invariant subspace angle.

studies.title: PCA correctness vs R prcomp — Powerhouse (CPU / fp64)
studies.note: CPU PCA vs R prcomp() on the canonical datasets (iris, USArrests; covariance and correlation scaling), identical float64 inputs, re-run on 5.0.0. Agreement is at LAPACK round-off and reproduces 4.4.1 BYTE-FOR-BYTE: sdev <=1.2e-15 relative, sign-aligned rotation <=6.1e-16, scores <=2.7e-12, explained-variance ratio <=4.4e-16. Both use SVD of the same centred/scaled matrix. (R wall is ~0 — prcomp on 50-150 rows is below R's timer resolution; the speed claim is the dedicated CPU-speed study.)

studies.title: PCA hard-case correctness — behaviour match vs R (R10) + defaults (R15)
studies.note: Adversarial grid (RIGOR R10), re-run on 5.0.0 and reproducing 4.4.1 byte-for-byte: pystatistics matches R's BEHAVIOUR, not only easy-data numbers. Near-collinear (cond~1e8), rank-deficient, and wide p>>n: sdev agrees to <=2.4e-15 and resolvable eigenvectors to <=1.5e-14; the near-collinear smallest singular value (7e-9) is recovered to machine precision (CPU SVD-of-X never squares the condition number). One null-space direction per degenerate design is correctly identified as ambiguous (excluded from the eigenvector comparison). A constant column under scale=TRUE is REFUSED by both engines (matched); under scale=FALSE both succeed. The default invocation pca(X) (center=True, scale=False) is the scale=False agreement case (R15).

studies.title: Factor analysis correctness vs R factanal — 1/2/3-factor (F1+F2 cleared at 4.4.1)
studies.note: ML factor analysis vs R factanal across 1-factor (iris), 2-factor (synth2f) and 3-factor (synth3f) models, re-run on 5.0.0 and reproducing 4.4.1 BYTE-FOR-BYTE. Uniquenesses, the ML objective and chi-squared are rotation-invariant (compared directly); loadings are compared up to column permutation + sign. Agreement: uniquenesses <=2.5e-5 absolute, loadings <=1.0e-5, objective <=3.2e-8 relative. The default multi-factor factor_analysis(X, n_factors>=2) (varimax) converges (F1, cleared at 4.4.1) and the lower=0.005 uniqueness floor matches factanal (F2, cleared at 4.4.1) — both unchanged in 5.0.0.

studies.title: CPU vs R across sizes — Powerhouse (priority 3: CPU must never lag R)
studies.note: The first-class CPU-speed deliverable (RIGOR priority 3 / R1), re-run on 5.0.0. PCA: pystatistics CPU MEETS-OR-BEATS R prcomp across n 1e3-1e5 and p 10-500 (speedup 1.26-1.70x at the resolvable sizes; the tiny n=1e4/p=10 point is timer-quantised at ~2ms), matching empirical complexity (~O(n^0.9) both engines). FA (rotation='none', both engines): pystatistics beats factanal 1.9-2.7x at n>=2000; the single small-n lag (n=500, ~0.6x) is the documented F3 / R2 cost — ~38 ML optimiser iterations on the noisier small-sample correlation vs ~10 at scale, a data-dependent iteration count, and R's sub-5ms times are timer-quantised. BLAS: numpy and R both on Apple Accelerate. No complexity-class gap (R1); profile matches 4.4.1 within timing variance.

studies.title: MPS PCA value — CPU vs MPS randomized (priority 4: the GPU must earn its place)
studies.note: The MPS randomized PCA path re-measured live on 5.0.0: materially faster than the fp64 CPU in its large regime — 2.9x at 100kx100, 9.8x at 500kx200, 28x at the wide 2000x5000 — with small-n (5000x100) at parity/near-parity (the expected dispatch-overhead regime, timing-variance sensitive point-to-point). Consistent with the 4.4.1 profile (3.5x / 9.3x / 31x) within GPU timing/thermal variance; the capability and its large-regime win are unchanged.

studies.title: MPS PCA correctness @ fp32 tier + fail-loud guards (R12/R13)
studies.note: MPS randomized vs the fp64 CPU reference, by the rotation-invariant subspace angle, re-measured on 5.0.0. Top-k subspace recovered to <=0.030 deg on tall/wide/square (sdev 3e-7..1.9e-4 depending on the spectral gap / n_iter), inside the GPU_FP32 statistical-equivalence tier; per-point numbers differ from 4.4.1 only at the documented fp32 GPU-reduction-nondeterminism level (same-seed not bit-identical), with the same per-point tier classification. The run also confirms the fail-loud guards (explicit solver='svd'/'gram' on MPS raise — no silent CPU fallback) and the no-silent-wrong gate (accepts ill-conditioned full matrices whose retained top-k is well-conditioned and is correct there; refuses when the retained top-k is ill-conditioned, with cpu-escape and force-bypass) — see the run JSON 'guards' block.

studies.title: CF-1 fp32-Gram no-silent-wrong gate boundary — Forge (CUDA) (R12/R13) [carried forward]
studies.note: CARRIED FORWARD from v4.4.1 (5.0.0 is rename-only; Forge not attached to this host). Clears CARRY-FORWARD CF-1. The opt-in solver='gram' fp32 path forms X'X in single precision (the exact CF-1 defect class). Sweeping cond(X) across the fp32 gate, silent_wrong_count = 0: every ACCEPTED fp32 fit is correct vs fp64 (subspace ~0 deg, sdev ~3e-6); every design past the fp32-safe boundary REFUSES (NumericalError) with force=True the documented override. The randomized gate behaves identically (R13). The gate is a true classifier — never accepts a wrong fit (R12), never refuses a well-conditioned retained top-k.

studies.title: Precision-vs-hardware isolation — Forge: gpu_fp64 vs cpu_fp64 (R11) [carried forward]
studies.note: CARRIED FORWARD from v4.4.1 (5.0.0 is rename-only; Forge not attached to this host). GPU speedup attribution (RIGOR R11). The same-precision pivot gpu_fp64 vs cpu_fp64 isolates the hardware effect: gpu_fp64 is numerically EXACT vs CPU (~5e-14..2e-13) but SLOWER than CPU (hardware-only 0.06-0.65x) — the consumer RTX 5070 Ti runs fp64 at ~1/64 fp32. So the fp32 GPU win (bundled 2.2-7.3x) is driven by fp32 precision + the randomized algorithm, not raw double-precision hardware throughput. gpu_fp64 is a CPU-parity correctness option, not a speed path; reported honestly rather than as a bundled headline.

studies.title: CUDA randomized PCA — value + correctness (R13) [carried forward]
studies.note: CARRIED FORWARD from v4.4.1 (5.0.0 is rename-only; Forge not attached to this host). The randomized path re-proven on CUDA (R13 — a guarantee is regime-conditional; the MPS proof does not transfer for free). Subspace recovered to ~0 deg at every shape; faster than the fp64 CPU — 5.0x (100kx100), 9.0x (500kx200), 109x (wide 2000x5000).

record_fields.sdev_max_rel: max relative difference between pystatistics and the reference over the component standard deviations (PCA correctness headline)
record_fields.rotation_max_abs: max absolute difference over the sign-aligned loadings/rotation matrix
record_fields.scores_max_rel: max relative difference over the sign-aligned scores
record_fields.subspace_max_angle_deg: largest principal angle (degrees) between the pystatistics and reference top-k subspaces — the rotation-invariant correctness metric, immune to eigenvector ambiguity
record_fields.smallest_sdev_pystat: the smallest component standard deviation pystatistics recovered (CF-1 relevance: the CPU SVD-of-X path preserves it to machine precision even at cond~1e8)
record_fields.speedup_vs_r: R wall-clock / pystatistics wall-clock on the same fit (>1 means pystatistics is faster)
record_fields.mps_speedup_vs_cpu: fp64 CPU wall-clock / MPS randomized wall-clock (>1 means the GPU earns its place)
record_fields.hardware_only_speedup_fp64: cpu_fp64 wall / gpu_fp64 wall — the same-precision, hardware-only pivot (R11); <1 means the consumer GPU's crippled fp64 loses to the CPU
record_fields.accepted_correct: for an accepted fp32 fit: True iff it matches the fp64 reference (subspace<1deg AND sdev_rel<1e-2) — the no-silent-wrong check (R12)
record_fields.force_bypasses: for a refused design: True iff force=True bypasses the condition gate (the documented override)
